neighbours.label: 'is' / ''s' after existential 'there' (there is, there's)
fire: Near the old harbour there is a small market that sells fresh fish.
The house is cheap, but there is a crack running through the cellar wall.
In winter there is almost no daylight in the northern villages.
The town has one school, and there is also a tiny library.
Inside the box there's a letter and two faded photographs.
During the festival there is music in every square.
Behind the church there is a garden where monks grew herbs.
At the end of the trail there's a waterfall worth the climb.
quiet: Near the old harbour the market is small and sells fresh fish.
The house is cheap, but the cellar wall has a crack running through it.
In winter the daylight is almost gone in the northern villages.
The town has one school, and it is also home to a tiny library.
Inside the box it's dusty, with a letter and two faded photographs.
During the festival music fills every square.
Behind the church the garden is where monks grew herbs.
At the end of the trail it's a steep climb to the waterfall.
